minutes.headline: Sewer Commission backed an engineer's plan for a new grease trap at One Main Street, with camera checks and a review in six months.
minutes.summary: The commission heard a hired engineer say the existing interior grease trap is adequately sized but rusting and should be replaced, then voted to accept that recommendation with camera inspections and follow-up reviews. The business manager reported on the Leominster IMA negotiation, the FY25 budget, capital planning and rate increase, and the commission agreed to cancel the next regular meeting for an in-person budget workshop. Other items were the sewer billing software problem and public statement, and the business manager job description score.

budget_items.topic: Leominster IMA flow increase and rate
budget_items.what_was_said: Leominster would not agree to raise the permitted flow because Lunenburg uses well under its current allowance. Leominster proposed lower rates for FY25 and FY26 than its initial increase, then penny-for-penny increases.
The business manager and the DPW's Robert reviewed capital needs, mostly pump and generator replacement, over five years.
Worksheet assumes Leominster's FY25 rate then a further increase, with a placeholder local rate increase; the average residential quarterly bill would rise.
The forecast draws on retained earnings in the near years and starts adding to it by fiscal 29. A lower rate increase would mean a larger draw.

budget_items.topic: Sewer pump costs and Green Communities grant
budget_items.what_was_said: Pump replacements cost more than expected; a state energy representative indicated the grant program would fund pumps and drives, with an application planned in April.
Retained earnings certified at end of FY23 were reported alongside capital reserve stabilization, inflow/infiltration and capacity fund balances, the latter two being very low.
The five-year forecast carries an annual I&I line that may need to rise.
Members recalled a prior plan to give the DPW director funds for maintenance and keep a reserve, and discussed contributing annually to capital reserve.
Proposed capital maintenance line would cover emergency pump failures; drawing on the stabilization fund requires a town meeting vote.
Prices for pumps at Dana Street, Leominster Road and Mass One are still awaited and expected to be higher than thought.
A small share of second-quarter bills were overbilled and will be credited; many staff hours went into the issue.
The Personnel Committee raised the job description score after revisions.

decisions.decision: Next regular meeting cancelled; February 13 at 6 PM becomes an in-person budget workshop at the DPW, not recorded.
IMA revisions (debt service wording in section 19.2) to be circulated and a vote placed on the next meeting agenda.
Commission wants the former sewer advisor invited to a future meeting on inflow and infiltration.
Business manager and DPW director to ask the town manager to post the billing-delay notice in her own name; the commission will not state tax bill impact.
Business manager will schedule the six-month review after receiving the plumbing inspector's sign-off on the new trap.
A warrant article to allow stabilization fund draws for emergency expenses was floated; the business manager will talk to the town manager and accountant.
Upcoming meetings: Feb 13 workshop, then regular meetings Feb 27, Mar 12, Mar 26.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted by roll call to accept its engineer's recommendation to install a new grease trap at One Main Street.
The vote attaches a camera inspection after six months, an evaluation after one year and a status meeting in six months.
The business manager reported that Leominster would not raise Lunenburg's permitted flow, and offered lower FY25 and FY26 rates before later increases.
The commission cancelled its next regular meeting and set a February 13 in-person budget workshop at the DPW, which will not be recorded.
A small share of second-quarter sewer bills were overbilled and will be credited; the commission will not state any tax bill impact of the delay notice.

why_it_matters: Sewer rates are set partly by what Leominster charges Lunenburg, and the forecast assumes a rate increase and draws on retained earnings, so quarterly sewer bills are likely to rise.
Pump replacements cost more than expected and the reserve funds for inflow and infiltration are very low, so emergency repairs may need a town meeting vote on stabilization fund draws.
The February 13 budget workshop will not be recorded, so residents who want to follow the FY25 sewer budget would need to attend in person.
watch_next: February 13 at 6 PM: in-person budget workshop at the DPW, not recorded.
A vote on the revised Leominster IMA, including the debt service wording in section 19.2, is to be placed on a coming agenda; regular meetings follow Feb 27, Mar 12 and Mar 26.
